name: Vint
description: Vint ('Screw') is a Russian partnership trick-taking game that influenced Contract Bridge's development. 4 players in 2 teams. 52-card deck. 13 each. Bidding (1-7 tricks over 6) with suit/NT denominations. NO dummy — all play own hands. Both sides score below-the-line for tricks won. First to 500 wins.

history.origins: Vint emerged in Russia in the latter half of the 19th century; primitive forms were known as Siberian vint. It was fashionable in late 19th-century Russia and featured bidding and scoring that foreshadowed Contract Bridge. The Russian word Vint (винт) means 'screw', referring to the rotating auction. It declined after the revolution but survived in Finland as Skruuvi and reached North America, influencing Contract Bridge in the 1920s.
timeline: Late 19th century: Game emerged in Russia; primitive forms known as Siberian vint.
history.cultural: Was Russia's most popular card game before Bridge.

setup.dealing: The cards are shuffled and cut; 13 cards are dealt to each player, one at a time face down, clockwise.

rules.objective: Score points by winning tricks and making contracts; first partnership to reach 500 points below the line wins the game.
rules.gameplay: Bidding: 1-7 (tricks over 6). Denominations: ♠<♣<♦<♥<NT. 3 consecutive passes end auction. Declarer plays against defenders. NO dummy. Follow suit. Both sides score below-the-line for tricks. Honors, slams, undertricks scored above-the-line.

variations.emptyOverridesReason: No documented variations with overrides; add when sources provide them.

scoring.description: Below line: tricks × contract value. Above line: honors, slams, penalties. Both sides score for tricks. First to 500.
